blocks.source: Canto X
blocks.translation: Canto X

blocks.source: Ora sen va per un secreto calle,
blocks.translation: Now onward goes, along a narrow path

blocks.source: tra ’l muro de la terra e li martìri,
blocks.translation: Between the torments and the city wall,

blocks.source: lo mio maestro, e io dopo le spalle.
blocks.translation: My Master, and I follow at his back.

blocks.source: «O virtù somma, che per li empi giri
blocks.translation: “O power supreme, that through these impious circles

blocks.source: mi volvi», cominciai, «com’ a te piace,
blocks.translation: Turnest me,” I began, “as pleases thee,

blocks.source: parlami, e sodisfammi a’ miei disiri.
blocks.translation: Speak to me, and my longings satisfy;

blocks.source: La gente che per li sepolcri giace
blocks.translation: The people who are lying in these tombs,

blocks.source: potrebbesi veder? già son levati
blocks.translation: Might they be seen? already are uplifted

blocks.source: tutt’ i coperchi, e nessun guardia face».
blocks.translation: The covers all, and no one keepeth guard.”

blocks.source: E quelli a me: «Tutti saran serrati
blocks.translation: And he to me: “They all will be closed up

blocks.source: quando di Iosafàt qui torneranno
blocks.translation: When from Jehoshaphat they shall return

blocks.source: coi corpi che là sù hanno lasciati.
blocks.translation: Here with the bodies they have left above.

blocks.source: Suo cimitero da questa parte hanno
blocks.translation: Their cemetery have upon this side

blocks.source: con Epicuro tutti suoi seguaci,
blocks.translation: With Epicurus all his followers,

blocks.source: che l’anima col corpo morta fanno.
blocks.translation: Who with the body mortal make the soul;

blocks.source: Però a la dimanda che mi faci
blocks.translation: But in the question thou dost put to me,

blocks.source: quinc’ entro satisfatto sarà tosto,
blocks.translation: Within here shalt thou soon be satisfied,

blocks.source: e al disio ancor che tu mi taci».
blocks.translation: And likewise in the wish thou keepest silent.”

blocks.source: E io: «Buon duca, non tegno riposto
blocks.translation: And I: “Good Leader, I but keep concealed

blocks.source: a te mio cuor se non per dicer poco,
blocks.translation: From thee my heart, that I may speak the less,

blocks.source: e tu m’hai non pur mo a ciò disposto».
blocks.translation: Nor only now hast thou thereto disposed me.”

blocks.source: «O Tosco che per la città del foco
blocks.translation: “O Tuscan, thou who through the city of fire

blocks.source: vivo ten vai così parlando onesto,
blocks.translation: Goest alive, thus speaking modestly,

blocks.source: piacciati di restare in questo loco.
blocks.translation: Be pleased to stay thy footsteps in this place.

blocks.source: La tua loquela ti fa manifesto
blocks.translation: Thy mode of speaking makes thee manifest

blocks.source: di quella nobil patrïa natio,
blocks.translation: A native of that noble fatherland,

blocks.source: a la qual forse fui troppo molesto».
blocks.translation: To which perhaps I too molestful was.”

blocks.source: Subitamente questo suono uscìo
blocks.translation: Upon a sudden issued forth this sound

blocks.source: d’una de l’arche; però m’accostai,
blocks.translation: From out one of the tombs; wherefore I pressed,

blocks.source: temendo, un poco più al duca mio.
blocks.translation: Fearing, a little nearer to my Leader.

blocks.source: Ed el mi disse: «Volgiti! Che fai?
blocks.translation: And unto me he said: “Turn thee; what dost thou?

blocks.source: Vedi là Farinata che s’è dritto:
blocks.translation: Behold there Farinata who has risen;

blocks.source: da la cintola in sù tutto ’l vedrai».
blocks.translation: From the waist upwards wholly shalt thou see him.”

blocks.source: Io avea già il mio viso nel suo fitto;
blocks.translation: I had already fixed mine eyes on his,

blocks.source: ed el s’ergea col petto e con la fronte
blocks.translation: And he uprose erect with breast and front

blocks.source: com’ avesse l’inferno a gran dispitto.
blocks.translation: E’en as if Hell he had in great despite.

blocks.source: E l’animose man del duca e pronte
blocks.translation: And with courageous hands and prompt my Leader

blocks.source: mi pinser tra le sepulture a lui,
blocks.translation: Thrust me between the sepulchres towards him,

blocks.source: dicendo: «Le parole tue sien conte».
blocks.translation: Exclaiming, “Let thy words explicit be.”

blocks.source: Com’ io al piè de la sua tomba fui,
blocks.translation: As soon as I was at the foot of his tomb

blocks.source: guardommi un poco, e poi, quasi sdegnoso,
blocks.translation: Somewhat he eyed me, and, as if disdainful,

blocks.source: mi dimandò: «Chi fuor li maggior tui?».
blocks.translation: Then asked of me, “Who were thine ancestors?”

blocks.source: Io ch’era d’ubidir disideroso,
blocks.translation: I, who desirous of obeying was,

blocks.source: non gliel celai, ma tutto gliel’ apersi;
blocks.translation: Concealed it not, but all revealed to him;

blocks.source: ond’ ei levò le ciglia un poco in suso;
blocks.translation: Whereat he raised his brows a little upward.

blocks.source: poi disse: «Fieramente furo avversi
blocks.translation: Then said he: “Fiercely adverse have they been

blocks.source: a me e a miei primi e a mia parte,
blocks.translation: To me, and to my fathers, and my party;

blocks.source: sì che per due fïate li dispersi».
blocks.translation: So that two several times I scattered them.”

blocks.source: «S’ei fur cacciati, ei tornar d’ogne parte»,
blocks.translation: “If they were banished, they returned on all sides,”

blocks.source: rispuos’ io lui, «l’una e l’altra fïata;
blocks.translation: I answered him, “the first time and the second;

blocks.source: ma i vostri non appreser ben quell’ arte».
blocks.translation: But yours have not acquired that art aright.”

blocks.source: Allor surse a la vista scoperchiata
blocks.translation: Then there uprose upon the sight, uncovered

blocks.source: un’ombra, lungo questa, infino al mento:
blocks.translation: Down to the chin, a shadow at his side;

blocks.source: credo che s’era in ginocchie levata.
blocks.translation: I think that he had risen on his knees.

blocks.source: Dintorno mi guardò, come talento
blocks.translation: Round me he gazed, as if solicitude

blocks.source: avesse di veder s’altri era meco;
blocks.translation: He had to see if some one else were with me,

blocks.source: e poi che ’l sospecciar fu tutto spento,
blocks.translation: But after his suspicion was all spent,

blocks.source: piangendo disse: «Se per questo cieco
blocks.translation: Weeping, he said to me: “If through this blind

blocks.source: carcere vai per altezza d’ingegno,
blocks.translation: Prison thou goest by loftiness of genius,

blocks.source: mio figlio ov’ è? e perché non è teco?».
blocks.translation: Where is my son? and why is he not with thee?”

blocks.source: E io a lui: «Da me stesso non vegno:
blocks.translation: And I to him: “I come not of myself;

blocks.source: colui ch’attende là, per qui mi mena
blocks.translation: He who is waiting yonder leads me here,

blocks.source: forse cui Guido vostro ebbe a disdegno».
blocks.translation: Whom in disdain perhaps your Guido had.”

blocks.source: Le sue parole e ’l modo de la pena
blocks.translation: His language and the mode of punishment

blocks.source: m’avean di costui già letto il nome;
blocks.translation: Already unto me had read his name;

blocks.source: però fu la risposta così piena.
blocks.translation: On that account my answer was so full.

blocks.source: Di sùbito drizzato gridò: «Come?
blocks.translation: Up starting suddenly, he cried out: “How

blocks.source: dicesti “elli ebbe”? non viv’ elli ancora?
blocks.translation: Saidst thou,—he had?  Is he not still alive?

blocks.source: non fiere li occhi suoi lo dolce lume?».
blocks.translation: Does not the sweet light strike upon his eyes?”

blocks.source: Quando s’accorse d’alcuna dimora
blocks.translation: When he became aware of some delay,

blocks.source: ch’io facëa dinanzi a la risposta,
blocks.translation: Which I before my answer made, supine

blocks.source: supin ricadde e più non parve fora.
blocks.translation: He fell again, and forth appeared no more.

blocks.source: Ma quell’ altro magnanimo, a cui posta
blocks.translation: But the other, magnanimous, at whose desire

blocks.source: restato m’era, non mutò aspetto,
blocks.translation: I had remained, did not his aspect change,

blocks.source: né mosse collo, né piegò sua costa;
blocks.translation: Neither his neck he moved, nor bent his side.

blocks.source: e sé continüando al primo detto,
blocks.translation: “And if,” continuing his first discourse,

blocks.source: «S’elli han quell’ arte», disse, «male appresa,
blocks.translation: “They have that art,” he said, “not learned aright,

blocks.source: ciò mi tormenta più che questo letto.
blocks.translation: That more tormenteth me, than doth this bed.

blocks.source: Ma non cinquanta volte fia raccesa
blocks.translation: But fifty times shall not rekindled be

blocks.source: la faccia de la donna che qui regge,
blocks.translation: The countenance of the Lady who reigns here,

blocks.source: che tu saprai quanto quell’ arte pesa.
blocks.translation: Ere thou shalt know how heavy is that art;

blocks.source: E se tu mai nel dolce mondo regge,
blocks.translation: And as thou wouldst to the sweet world return,

blocks.source: dimmi: perché quel popolo è sì empio
blocks.translation: Say why that people is so pitiless

blocks.source: incontr’ a’ miei in ciascuna sua legge?».
blocks.translation: Against my race in each one of its laws?”

blocks.source: Ond’ io a lui: «Lo strazio e ’l grande scempio
blocks.translation: Whence I to him: “The slaughter and great carnage

blocks.source: che fece l’Arbia colorata in rosso,
blocks.translation: Which have with crimson stained the Arbia, cause

blocks.source: tal orazion fa far nel nostro tempio».
blocks.translation: Such orisons in our temple to be made.”

blocks.source: Poi ch’ebbe sospirando il capo mosso,
blocks.translation: After his head he with a sigh had shaken,

blocks.source: «A ciò non fu’ io sol», disse, «né certo
blocks.translation: “There I was not alone,” he said, “nor surely

blocks.source: sanza cagion con li altri sarei mosso.
blocks.translation: Without a cause had with the others moved.

blocks.source: Ma fu’ io solo, là dove sofferto
blocks.translation: But there I was alone, where every one

blocks.source: fu per ciascun di tòrre via Fiorenza,
blocks.translation: Consented to the laying waste of Florence,

blocks.source: colui che la difesi a viso aperto».
blocks.translation: He who defended her with open face.”

blocks.source: «Deh, se riposi mai vostra semenza»,
blocks.translation: “Ah! so hereafter may your seed repose,”

blocks.source: prega’ io lui, «solvetemi quel nodo
blocks.translation: I him entreated, “solve for me that knot,

blocks.source: che qui ha ’nviluppata mia sentenza.
blocks.translation: Which has entangled my conceptions here.

blocks.source: El par che voi veggiate, se ben odo,
blocks.translation: It seems that you can see, if I hear rightly,

blocks.source: dinanzi quel che ’l tempo seco adduce,
blocks.translation: Beforehand whatsoe’er time brings with it,

blocks.source: e nel presente tenete altro modo».
blocks.translation: And in the present have another mode.”

blocks.source: «Noi veggiam, come quei c’ha mala luce,
blocks.translation: “We see, like those who have imperfect sight,

blocks.source: le cose», disse, «che ne son lontano;
blocks.translation: The things,” he said, “that distant are from us;

blocks.source: cotanto ancor ne splende il sommo duce.
blocks.translation: So much still shines on us the Sovereign Ruler.

blocks.source: Quando s’appressano o son, tutto è vano
blocks.translation: When they draw near, or are, is wholly vain

blocks.source: nostro intelletto; e s’altri non ci apporta,
blocks.translation: Our intellect, and if none brings it to us,

blocks.source: nulla sapem di vostro stato umano.
blocks.translation: Not anything know we of your human state.

blocks.source: Però comprender puoi che tutta morta
blocks.translation: Hence thou canst understand, that wholly dead

blocks.source: fia nostra conoscenza da quel punto
blocks.translation: Will be our knowledge from the moment when

blocks.source: che del futuro fia chiusa la porta».
blocks.translation: The portal of the future shall be closed.”

blocks.source: Allor, come di mia colpa compunto,
blocks.translation: Then I, as if compunctious for my fault,

blocks.source: dissi: «Or direte dunque a quel caduto
blocks.translation: Said: “Now, then, you will tell that fallen one,

blocks.source: che ’l suo nato è co’ vivi ancor congiunto;
blocks.translation: That still his son is with the living joined.

blocks.source: e s’i’ fui, dianzi, a la risposta muto,
blocks.translation: And if just now, in answering, I was dumb,

blocks.source: fate i saper che ’l fei perché pensava
blocks.translation: Tell him I did it because I was thinking

blocks.source: già ne l’error che m’avete soluto».
blocks.translation: Already of the error you have solved me.”

blocks.source: E già ’l maestro mio mi richiamava;
blocks.translation: And now my Master was recalling me,

blocks.source: per ch’i’ pregai lo spirto più avaccio
blocks.translation: Wherefore more eagerly I prayed the spirit

blocks.source: che mi dicesse chi con lu’ istava.
blocks.translation: That he would tell me who was with him there.

blocks.source: Dissemi: «Qui con più di mille giaccio:
blocks.translation: He said: “With more than a thousand here I lie;

blocks.source: qua dentro è ’l secondo Federico
blocks.translation: Within here is the second Frederick,

blocks.source: e ’l Cardinale; e de li altri mi taccio».
blocks.translation: And the Cardinal, and of the rest I speak not.”

blocks.source: Indi s’ascose; e io inver’ l’antico
blocks.translation: Thereon he hid himself; and I towards

blocks.source: poeta volsi i passi, ripensando
blocks.translation: The ancient poet turned my steps, reflecting

blocks.source: a quel parlar che mi parea nemico.
blocks.translation: Upon that saying, which seemed hostile to me.

blocks.source: Elli si mosse; e poi, così andando,
blocks.translation: He moved along; and afterward thus going,

blocks.source: mi disse: «Perché se’ tu sì smarrito?».
blocks.translation: He said to me, “Why art thou so bewildered?”

blocks.source: E io li sodisfeci al suo dimando.
blocks.translation: And I in his inquiry satisfied him.

blocks.source: «La mente tua conservi quel ch’udito
blocks.translation: “Let memory preserve what thou hast heard

blocks.source: hai contra te», mi comandò quel saggio;
blocks.translation: Against thyself,” that Sage commanded me,

blocks.source: «e ora attendi qui», e drizzò ’l dito:
blocks.translation: “And now attend here;” and he raised his finger.

blocks.source: «quando sarai dinanzi al dolce raggio
blocks.translation: “When thou shalt be before the radiance sweet

blocks.source: di quella il cui bell’ occhio tutto vede,
blocks.translation: Of her whose beauteous eyes all things behold,

blocks.source: da lei saprai di tua vita il vïaggio».
blocks.translation: From her thou’lt know the journey of thy life.”

blocks.source: Appresso mosse a man sinistra il piede:
blocks.translation: Unto the left hand then he turned his feet;

blocks.source: lasciammo il muro e gimmo inver’ lo mezzo
blocks.translation: We left the wall, and went towards the middle,

blocks.source: per un sentier ch’a una valle fiede,
blocks.translation: Along a path that strikes into a valley,

blocks.source: che ’nfin là sù facea spiacer suo lezzo.
blocks.translation: Which even up there unpleasant made its stench.
